segments.ipa: /haʊ əˈbaʊt ju/

segments.text: Follow their invitation.
segments.ipa: /ˈfɑloʊ ðɛr ˌɪnvɪˈteɪʃən/

segments.text: Tell them one little thing that happened and let the conversation grow from there.
segments.ipa: /tɛl ðɛm wʌn ˈlɪtəl θɪŋ ðæt ˈhæpənd ənd lɛt ðə ˌkɑnvərˈseɪʃən ɡroʊ frʌm ðɛr/

segments.text: That reminds me of my friend Ben.
segments.ipa: /ðæt riˈmaɪndz mi ʌv maɪ frɛnd bɛn/

segments.text: He said nothing much.
segments.ipa: /hi sɛd ˈnʌθɪŋ mʌtʃ/

segments.text: But when I mentioned my cooking disaster, he suddenly had plenty to say.
segments.ipa: /bʌt wɛn aɪ ˈmɛnʃənd maɪ ˈkʊkɪŋ dɪˈzæstər hi ˈsʌdənli hæd ˈplɛnti tu seɪ/

segments.text: Apparently, everybody has an opinion about burnt pasta. Burnt pasta?
segments.ipa: /əˈpɛrəntli ˈɛvriˌbɑdi hæz æn əˈpɪnjən əˈbaʊt bɝnt ˈpɑstə bɝnt ˈpɑstə/

segments.text: I've got questions.
segments.ipa: /aɪv ɡɑt ˈkwɛstʃənz/

segments.text: But first, invite Ben to dinner somewhere with a professional kitchen.
segments.ipa: /bʌt fɝst ˌɪnˈvaɪt bɛn tu ˈdɪnər ˈsʌmˌwɛr wɪð ə prəˈfɛʃənəl ˈkɪtʃən/

segments.text: You've started talking.
segments.ipa: /juv ˈstɑrtɪd ˈtɔkɪŋ/

segments.text: How do you turn that conversation into an actual plan?
segments.ipa: /haʊ du ju tɝn ðæt ˌkɑnvərˈseɪʃən ˈɪntu æn ˈæktʃəwəl plæn/

segments.text: Preferably without offering to cook.
segments.ipa: /ˈprɛfərəbli wɪˈθaʊt ˈɔfərɪŋ tu kʊk/

segments.text: I'd say, "Want to grab a coffee this weekend? It's friendly. It's simple.
segments.ipa: /aɪd seɪ wɑnt tu ɡræb ə ˈkɑfi ðɪs ˈwiˌkɛnd ɪts ˈfrɛndli ɪts ˈsɪmpəl/

segments.text: And Ben can picture what I'm inviting him to do." Exactly.
segments.ipa: /ənd bɛn kæn ˈpɪktʃər wʌt aɪm ˌɪnˈvaɪtɪŋ hɪm tu du ɪɡˈzæktli/

segments.text: Grab a coffee means get a coffee together.
segments.ipa: /ɡræb ə ˈkɑfi minz ɡɛt ə ˈkɑfi təˈɡɛðər/

segments.text: Nobody's asking you to run into a cafe, steal a cup, and escape.
segments.ipa: /ˈnoʊˌbɑˌdiz ˈæskɪŋ ju tu rʌn ˈɪntu ə kəˈfeɪ stil ə kʌp ənd ɪˈskeɪp/

segments.text: It's just a casual invitation.
segments.ipa: /ɪts dʒʌst ə ˈkæʒəwəl ˌɪnvɪˈteɪʃən/

segments.text: A much calmer afternoon.
segments.ipa: /ə mʌtʃ ˈkɑmər ˌæftərˈnun/

segments.text: And wanna is how want to often sounds in relaxed speech.
segments.ipa: /ənd ˈwɑnə ɪz haʊ wɑnt tu ˈɔfən saʊndz ɪn rɪˈlækst spitʃ/

segments.text: You can also say, "Do you want to grab a coffee?" Both work.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn ˈɔlsoʊ seɪ du ju wɑnt tu ɡræb ə ˈkɑfi boʊθ wɝk/

segments.text: I also like, "Are you free on Saturday?"
segments.ipa: /aɪ ˈɔlsoʊ laɪk ɑr ju fri ɑn ˈsætərdi/

segments.text: But I'd add the reason fairly quickly.
segments.ipa: /bʌt aɪd æd ðə ˈrizən ˈfɛrli ˈkwɪkli/

segments.text: Otherwise, your friend might wonder whether you need help moving a sofa.
segments.ipa: /ˈʌðərˌwaɪz jɔr frɛnd maɪt ˈwʌndər ˈwɛðər ju nid hɛlp ˈmuvɪŋ ə ˈsoʊfə/

segments.text: That's why I sometimes lead with the activity.
segments.ipa: /ðæts waɪ aɪ səmˈtaɪmz lɛd wɪð ðə ækˈtɪvəti/

segments.text: I'm going for a walk Saturday morning.
segments.ipa: /aɪm ˈɡoʊɪŋ fɔr ə wɔk ˈsætərdi ˈmɔrnɪŋ/

segments.text: Want to come?
segments.ipa: /wɑnt tu kʌm/

segments.text: They know what they're saying yes to.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ noʊ wʌt ðɛr ˈseɪɪŋ jɛs tu/

segments.text: And joining something you're already doing can feel easy, but would you use that invitation for a friend you haven't seen in months? Sure.
segments.ipa: /ənd ˈdʒɔɪnɪŋ ˈsʌmθɪŋ jʊr ɔlˈrɛdi ˈduɪŋ kæn fil ˈizi bʌt wʊd ju jus ðæt ˌɪnvɪˈteɪʃən fɔr ə frɛnd ju ˈhævənt sin ɪn mʌnθs ʃʊr/

segments.text: Though I'd make it warmer.
segments.ipa: /ðoʊ aɪd meɪk ɪt ˈwɔrmər/

segments.text: I'd love to catch up.
segments.ipa: /aɪd lʌv tu kætʃ ʌp/

segments.text: Are you free for a walk Saturday morning?
segments.ipa: /ɑr ju fri fɔr ə wɔk ˈsætərdi ˈmɔrnɪŋ/

segments.text: That tells them I'm interested in their company.
segments.ipa: /ðæt tɛlz ðɛm aɪm ˈɪntrəstɪd ɪn ðɛr ˈkʌmpəˌni/

segments.text: I like that.
segments.ipa: /aɪ laɪk ðæt/

segments.text: Catch up means talk about what's happened since you last spent time together.
segments.ipa: /kætʃ ʌp minz tɔk əˈbaʊt wʌts ˈhæpənd sɪns ju læst spɛnt taɪm təˈɡɛðər/

segments.text: It gives the invitation a personal reason without making it a big speech.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ɡɪvz ðə ˌɪnvɪˈteɪʃən ə ˈpɝsɪnəl ˈrizən wɪˈθaʊt ˈmeɪkɪŋ ɪt ə bɪɡ spitʃ/

segments.text: What about something at home?
segments.ipa: /wʌt əˈbaʊt ˈsʌmθɪŋ æt hoʊm/

segments.text: Want to come over and watch a movie?
segments.ipa: /wɑnt tu kʌm ˈoʊvər ənd wɑtʃ ə ˈmuvi/

segments.text: That's another useful invitation, although I should probably promise there won't be pasta.
segments.ipa: /ðæts əˈnʌðər ˈjusfəl ˌɪnvɪˈteɪʃən ˌɔlˈðoʊ aɪ ʃʊd ˈprɑbəˌbli ˈprɑməs ðɛr woʊnt bi ˈpɑstə/

segments.text: Your reputation may need time.
segments.ipa: /jɔr ˌrɛpjəˈteɪʃən meɪ nid taɪm/

segments.text: Come over means visit your home.
segments.ipa: /kʌm ˈoʊvər minz ˈvɪzɪt jɔr hoʊm/

segments.text: And if it's a group, a few of us are watching a movie Friday.
segments.ipa: /ənd ɪf ɪts ə ɡrup ə fju ʌv ʌs ɑr ˈwɑtʃɪŋ ə ˈmuvi ˈfraɪdi/

segments.text: Want to join us? Works well.
segments.ipa: /wɑnt tu dʒɔɪn ʌs wɝks wɛl/

segments.text: That also helps someone understand the situation.
segments.ipa: /ðæt ˈɔlsoʊ hɛlps ˈsʌmˌwʌn ˌʌndərˈstænd ðə ˌsɪtʃuˈeɪʃən/

segments.text: A quiet evening with one friend feels different from walking into a room with 12 people and three birthday cakes.
segments.ipa: /ə ˈkwaɪət ˈivnɪŋ wɪð wʌn frɛnd filz ˈdɪfərənt frʌm ˈwɔkɪŋ ˈɪntu ə rum wɪð ˈpipəl ənd θri ˈbɝθˌdeɪ keɪks/

segments.text: Three cakes could help though.
segments.ipa: /θri keɪks kʊd hɛlp ðoʊ/

segments.text: Give the details that matter, but you don't need to send a full event program.
segments.ipa: /ɡɪv ðə dɪˈteɪlz ðæt ˈmætər bʌt ju doʊnt nid tu sɛnd ə fʊl ɪˈvɛnt ˈproʊˌɡræm/

segments.text: Activity, possible day, and who's coming are often enough.
segments.ipa: /ækˈtɪvəti ˈpɑsəbəl deɪ ənd huz ˈkʌmɪŋ ɑr ˈɔfən ɪˈnʌf/

segments.text: Let's give listeners a moment to try it.
segments.ipa: /lɛts ɡɪv ˈlɪsənərz ə ˈmoʊmənt tu traɪ ɪt/

segments.text: Think of a friend and one thing you'd enjoy doing together.
segments.ipa: /θɪŋk ʌv ə frɛnd ənd wʌn θɪŋ jud ˌɛnˈdʒɔɪ ˈduɪŋ təˈɡɛðər/

segments.text: Pause the video now and say your invitation out loud. Welcome back.
segments.ipa: /pɔz ðə ˈvɪdioʊ naʊ ənd seɪ jɔr ˌɪnvɪˈteɪʃən aʊt laʊd ˈwɛlkəm bæk/

segments.text: Maybe you said, "Want to get lunch on Sunday?" Great.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ju sɛd wɑnt tu ɡɛt lʌntʃ ɑn ˈsʌnˌdeɪ ɡreɪt/

segments.text: Your invitation doesn't need fancy English.
segments.ipa: /jɔr ˌɪnvɪˈteɪʃən ˈdʌzənt nid ˈfænsi ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ/

segments.text: And tell us in the comments what you'd invite your friend to do.
segments.ipa: /ənd tɛl ʌs ɪn ðə ˈkɑmɛnts wʌt jud ˌɪnˈvaɪt jɔr frɛnd tu du/

segments.text: I'm hoping somebody says mini golf.
segments.ipa: /aɪm ˈhoʊpɪŋ ˈsʌmˌbɑdi sɛz ˈmɪni ɡɑlf/

segments.text: If these conversations help you practice, give the video a like and subscribe to Mr. English Channel.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ðiz ˌkɑnvərˈseɪʃənz hɛlp ju ˈpræktəs ɡɪv ðə ˈvɪdioʊ ə laɪk ənd səbˈskraɪb tu ˈmɪstər ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈtʃænəl/

segments.text: Then we can keep practicing together.
segments.ipa: /ðɛn wi kæn kip ˈpræktəsɪŋ təˈɡɛðər/

segments.text: Miniolf sounds fun, but now we've reached the part your group chat struggles with.
segments.ipa: /Miniolf saʊndz fʌn bʌt naʊ wiv ritʃt ðə pɑrt jɔr ɡrup tʃæt ˈstrʌɡəlz wɪð/

segments.text: Your friend says yes.
segments.ipa: /jɔr frɛnd sɛz jɛs/

segments.text: How do you choose a time without exchanging messages all afternoon?
segments.ipa: /haʊ du ju tʃuz ə taɪm wɪˈθaʊt ɪksˈtʃeɪndʒɪŋ ˈmɛsədʒəz ɔl ˌæftərˈnun/

segments.text: I'd offer something specific.
segments.ipa: /aɪd ˈɔfər ˈsʌmθɪŋ spəˈsɪfɪk/

segments.text: How about Saturday at 10:00?
segments.ipa: /haʊ əˈbaʊt ˈsætərdi æt/

segments.text: That's easier to answer than when are you free?
segments.ipa: /ðæts ˈiziər tu ˈænsər ðæn wɛn ɑr ju fri/

segments.text: Especially with six people checking six different calendars. Usually, yes.
segments.ipa: /əˈspɛʃli wɪð sɪks ˈpipəl ˈtʃɛkɪŋ sɪks ˈdɪfərənt ˈkæləndərz ˈjuʒəwəli jɛs/

segments.text: But if you know they work weekends, asking about their schedule first makes sense.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ɪf ju noʊ ðeɪ wɝk ˈwiˌkɛndz ˈæskɪŋ əˈbaʊt ðɛr ˈskɛdʒʊl fɝst meɪks sɛns/

segments.text: What day works for you?
segments.ipa: /wʌt deɪ wɝks fɔr ju/

segments.text: Shows you're considering their situation. Good point.
segments.ipa: /ʃoʊz jʊr kənˈsɪdərɪŋ ðɛr ˌsɪtʃuˈeɪʃən ɡʊd pɔɪnt/

segments.text: A clear suggestion helps, but it shouldn't ignore what you already know.
segments.ipa: /ə klɪr səˈdʒɛstʃən hɛlps bʌt ɪt ˈʃʊdənt ˌɪɡˈnɔr wʌt ju ɔlˈrɛdi noʊ/

segments.text: Suppose you suggest 10 and I say, "Could we make it 11?"
segments.ipa: /səˈpoʊz ju səˈdʒɛst ənd aɪ seɪ kʊd wi meɪk ɪt/

segments.text: I'd say 11 works for me.
segments.ipa: /aɪd seɪ wɝks fɔr mi/

segments.text: Could we make it 11?
segments.ipa: /kʊd wi meɪk ɪt/

segments.text: Is a natural way to suggest a different time.
segments.ipa: /ɪz ə ˈnætʃərəl weɪ tu səˈdʒɛst ə ˈdɪfərənt taɪm/

segments.text: You're helping shape the plan.
segments.ipa: /jʊr ˈhɛlpɪŋ ʃeɪp ðə plæn/

segments.text: And if 11's too late, you can say, "I need to leave by noon.
segments.ipa: /ənd ɪf ɛs tu leɪt ju kæn seɪ aɪ nid tu liv baɪ nun/

segments.text: Would 10:30 work?"
segments.ipa: /wʊd wɝk/

segments.text: Give a little reason and another possibility.
segments.ipa: /ɡɪv ə ˈlɪtəl ˈrizən ənd əˈnʌðər ˌpɑsəˈbɪləˌti/

segments.text: That's much easier to work with than just no.
segments.ipa: /ðæts mʌtʃ ˈiziər tu wɝk wɪð ðæn dʒʌst noʊ/

segments.text: Let's try a short example.
segments.ipa: /lɛts traɪ ə ʃɔrt ɪɡˈzæmpəl/

segments.text: I'll invite you and you'll help me choose the details. Ready? Ready.
segments.ipa: /aɪl ˌɪnˈvaɪt ju ənd jul hɛlp mi tʃuz ðə dɪˈteɪlz ˈrɛdi ˈrɛdi/

segments.text: I've checked my imaginary calendar and it's surprisingly empty. Go ahead.
segments.ipa: /aɪv tʃɛkt maɪ ˌɪˈmædʒəˌnɛri ˈkæləndər ənd ɪts sərˈpraɪzɪŋli ˈɛmpti ɡoʊ əˈhɛd/

segments.text: Hey, want to get lunch on Saturday?
segments.ipa: /heɪ wɑnt tu ɡɛt lʌntʃ ɑn ˈsætərdi/

segments.text: There's a new sandwich place near the station.
segments.ipa: /ðɛrz ə nu ˈsændwɪtʃ pleɪs nɪr ðə ˈsteɪʃən/

segments.text: Yeah, sounds good.
segments.ipa: /jæ saʊndz ɡʊd/

segments.text: What time are you thinking?
segments.ipa: /wʌt taɪm ɑr ju ˈθɪŋkɪŋ/

segments.text: How about 12:30?
segments.ipa: /haʊ əˈbaʊt/

segments.text: We could meet outside the station.
segments.ipa: /wi kʊd mit ˈaʊtˈsaɪd ðə ˈsteɪʃən/

segments.text: Could we make it 1:00?
segments.ipa: /kʊd wi meɪk ɪt/

segments.text: I've got something to do in the morning. One works.
segments.ipa: /aɪv ɡɑt ˈsʌmθɪŋ tu du ɪn ðə ˈmɔrnɪŋ wʌn wɝks/

segments.text: Let's meet by the main entrance.
segments.ipa: /lɛts mit baɪ ðə meɪn ˈɛntrəns/

segments.text: That's the end of our example.
segments.ipa: /ðæts ðə ɛnd ʌv ˈaʊər ɪɡˈzæmpəl/

segments.text: We agreed on the activity, the time, and a clear meeting place.
segments.ipa: /wi əˈɡrid ɑn ðə ækˈtɪvəti ðə taɪm ənd ə klɪr ˈmitɪŋ pleɪs/

segments.text: The clear place matters.
segments.ipa: /ðə klɪr pleɪs ˈmætərz/

segments.text: Near the station might leave me walking around three streets.
segments.ipa: /nɪr ðə ˈsteɪʃən maɪt liv mi ˈwɔkɪŋ ərˈaʊnd θri strits/

segments.text: By the main entrance gives me something I can actually find. Exactly.
segments.ipa: /baɪ ðə meɪn ˈɛntrəns ɡɪvz mi ˈsʌmθɪŋ aɪ kæn ˈækˌtʃuəli faɪnd ɪɡˈzæktli/

segments.text: Now, what if we agree on a time, but want different activities?
segments.ipa: /naʊ wʌt ɪf wi əˈɡri ɑn ə taɪm bʌt wɑnt ˈdɪfərənt ækˈtɪvətiz/

segments.text: You want mini golf and I want a quiet cafe where we can talk.
segments.ipa: /ju wɑnt ˈmɪni ɡɑlf ənd aɪ wɑnt ə ˈkwaɪət kəˈfeɪ wɛr wi kæn tɔk/

segments.text: I could suggest, how about coffee first than mini golf?
segments.ipa: /aɪ kʊd səˈdʒɛst haʊ əˈbaʊt ˈkɑfi fɝst ðæn ˈmɪni ɡɑlf/

segments.text: But that only works if we've both got time and actually want to do both, right?
segments.ipa: /bʌt ðæt ˈoʊnli wɝks ɪf wiv boʊθ ɡɑt taɪm ənd ˈækˌtʃuəli wɑnt tu du boʊθ raɪt/

segments.text: Combining ideas isn't always the answer.
segments.ipa: /kəmˈbaɪnɪŋ aɪˈdiəz ˈɪzənt ˈɔlˌweɪz ðə ˈænsər/

segments.text: I might say, "I'd rather do something quiet today.
segments.ipa: /aɪ maɪt seɪ aɪd ˈræðər du ˈsʌmθɪŋ ˈkwaɪət təˈdeɪ/

segments.text: Could we save mini golf for another weekend?"
segments.ipa: /kʊd wi seɪv ˈmɪni ɡɑlf fɔr əˈnʌðər ˈwiˌkɛnd/

segments.text: I'd appreciate knowing that.
segments.ipa: /aɪd əˈpriʃiˌeɪt ˈnoʊɪŋ ðæt/

segments.text: Otherwise, we could spend an hour saying anything's fine while secretly hoping the other person guesses what we want.
segments.ipa: /ˈʌðərˌwaɪz wi kʊd spɛnd æn ˈaʊər ˈseɪɪŋ ˈɛniˌθɪŋz faɪn waɪl ˈsikrɪtli ˈhoʊpɪŋ ðə ˈʌðər ˈpɝsən ˈɡɛsəz wʌt wi wɑnt/

segments.text: Being flexible doesn't mean having no preferences.
segments.ipa: /ˈbiɪŋ ˈflɛksəbəl ˈdʌzənt min ˈhævɪŋ noʊ ˈprɛfərənsɪz/

segments.text: You can say, "I'd prefer somewhere nearby."
segments.ipa: /ju kæn seɪ aɪd prəˈfɝ ˈsʌmˌwɛr ˈnɪrˈbaɪ/

segments.text: Or something inexpensive would be great.
segments.ipa: /ɔr ˈsʌmθɪŋ ˌɪnɪkˈspɛnsɪv wʊd bi ɡreɪt/

segments.text: That helps everyone choose.
segments.ipa: /ðæt hɛlps ˈɛvriˌwʌn tʃuz/

segments.text: Especially in my sixperson group.
segments.ipa: /əˈspɛʃli ɪn maɪ sixperson ɡrup/

segments.text: One friend wants dinner, another wants a walk, and someone keeps suggesting a place that's an hour away.
segments.ipa: /wʌn frɛnd wɑnts ˈdɪnər əˈnʌðər wɑnts ə wɔk ənd ˈsʌmˌwʌn kips səˈdʒɛstɪŋ ə pleɪs ðæts æn ˈaʊər əˈweɪ/

segments.text: We need a plan people can actually join.
segments.ipa: /wi nid ə plæn ˈpipəl kæn ˈækˌtʃuəli dʒɔɪn/

segments.text: Try giving the group two choices.
segments.ipa: /traɪ ˈɡɪvɪŋ ðə ɡrup tu ˈtʃɔɪsəz/

segments.text: Would you rather get lunch nearby or meet at the park?

segments.text: And once we've decided, I can write, "Okay, Saturday at 1 outside the cafe."

segments.text: And after all that organizing, someone wakes up with a terrible cold.

segments.text: Life has a way of changing even the clearest plan.

segments.text: What would you want that friend to tell you? Something direct.

segments.text: Hey, I'm sorry, but I'm not feeling well.

segments.text: I can't make it today.

segments.text: I'd rather know early than sit at the cafe wondering where they are.
segments.ipa: /aɪd ˈræðər noʊ ˈɝli ðæn sɪt æt ðə kəˈfeɪ ˈwʌndərɪŋ wɛr ðeɪ ɑr/

segments.text: gives you a little breathing room as long as you actually send that message.

segments.text: A reminder can help.

segments.text: And if you're the person receiving the cancellation, no worries.

segments.text: Hope you feel better is a kind response when someone's sick.

segments.text: What if you're disappointed though?
segments.ipa: /wʌt ɪf jʊr ˌdɪsəˈpɔɪntɪd ðoʊ/

segments.text: Do you have to pretend you're happy? No.

segments.ipa: /ju kæn bi wɔrm ənd ˈɑnəst/

segments.text: Let's pick a day that works better, that shares your feelings without making an accusation.
segments.ipa: /lɛts pɪk ə deɪ ðæt wɝks ˈbɛtər ðæt ʃɛrz jɔr ˈfilɪŋz wɪˈθaʊt ˈmeɪkɪŋ æn ˌækjəˈzeɪʃən/

segments.text: That feels fair.
segments.ipa: /ðæt filz fɛr/

segments.text: And if it keeps happening, I'd talk about it privately.
segments.ipa: /ənd ɪf ɪt kips ˈhæpənɪŋ aɪd tɔk əˈbaʊt ɪt ˈpraɪvətli/

segments.text: We've had trouble finding a time.
segments.ipa: /wiv hæd ˈtrʌbəl ˈfaɪndɪŋ ə taɪm/

segments.text: Is there an easier way for us to catch up? Exactly.
segments.ipa: /ɪz ðɛr æn ˈiziər weɪ fɔr ʌs tu kætʃ ʌp ɪɡˈzæktli/

segments.text: Maybe a long dinner is difficult, but a short walk fits.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ə lɔŋ ˈdɪnər ɪz ˈdɪfəkəlt bʌt ə ʃɔrt wɔk fɪts/

segments.ipa: /æsk bɪˈfɔr ˌdɪˈsaɪdɪŋ jɔr frɛnd ˈdʌzənt kɛr/

segments.text: Their schedule might be more complicated than you realize.
segments.ipa: /ðɛr ˈskɛdʒʊl maɪt bi mɔr ˈkɑmpləˌkeɪtəd ðæn ju ˈriəˌlaɪz/

segments.text: But we can also say no to an invitation without offering another date, right?

segments.text: Is clear and friendly.

segments.text: That's not really my thing, but I'd love to get coffee soon is enough.

segments.text: Three of us can meet and we can see the others another time.
segments.ipa: /θri ʌv ʌs kæn mit ənd wi kæn si ðə ˈʌðərz əˈnʌðər taɪm/

segments.text: Yes, especially if you've been waiting for months.
segments.ipa: /jɛs əˈspɛʃli ɪf juv bɪn ˈweɪtɪŋ fɔr mʌnθs/

segments.text: Keep it friendly and open.

segments.text: Then Saturday can finally happen.
segments.ipa: /ðɛn ˈsætərdi kæn ˈfaɪnəli ˈhæpən/

segments.text: Honestly, I'd be happy sitting in the park with those friends and eating sandwiches.

segments.text: No tickets, no reservations, no complicated schedule.

segments.text: It might be hearing how someone's doing or laughing about a story you both remember or discovering they also burned pasta.

segments.text: They're easier to repeat.
segments.ipa: /ðɛr ˈiziər tu rɪˈpit/

segments.text: I like that.
segments.ipa: /aɪ laɪk ðæt/

segments.text: Does ordinary time really feel like enough?

segments.text: Sometimes it does.
segments.ipa: /səmˈtaɪmz ɪt dʌz/

segments.text: We don't always need a special event to feel close.
segments.ipa: /wi doʊnt ˈɔlˌweɪz nid ə ˈspɛʃəl ɪˈvɛnt tu fil kloʊs/

segments.text: And we can ask, "Do you have time for a quick walk?"
segments.ipa: /ənd wi kæn æsk du ju hæv taɪm fɔr ə kwɪk wɔk/

segments.text: A little time still counts.
